samples.summary: The row-height write path (`Doc.setRowHeight`) is not normalized, so the model/CRDT can hold an out-of-band height while every reader clamps it — the resize drag silently stops honouring input at the ceiling and stored state diverges from rendered geometry
samples.evidence: `setRowHeight` stores `height` verbatim (`td.rowHeights[rowIndex] = height;` then `updateTableAttrs`). The only caller, `packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:2227-2229`, computes `newHeight = Math.max(currentHeight + deltaPx, 20)` where `currentHeight = tl.rowHeights[drag.index]` is the *already-clamped* layout value. Once a row's stored height passes MAX_ROW_HEIGHT (10000), each further downward drag writes 10000+delta but the layout re-clamps to 10000, so the row appears frozen while the persisted value keeps growing, and the value broadcast to peers is one no reader will honour. Normalizing at the write (as `normalizeRowHeight` already does for readers) would keep the stored value and the geometry in agreement. Contrast `listLevel`, which is normalized at each point of use *and* whose writers stay in band.
searchedFor: grep setRowHeight (repo-wide) — only document.ts:1177 and text-editor.ts:2229
grep rowHeights in packages/docs, packages/frontend, packages/backend

samples.summary: Per-row clamp leaves the aggregate pagination cost unbounded: each clamped row still expands to ~12 pages, so a table with many rows still multiplies page/PageLine count by ~500x over its content height
samples.evidence: MAX_ROW_HEIGHT = 10000 against a ~864px content height means one poisoned row still yields ~12 pages in `paginateLayout`'s `while (consumed < rowHeight)` loop (packages/docs/src/view/pagination.ts:124). Nothing bounds the number of poisoned rows: a `rowHeights` attribute with N entries against N cheap rows gives ~12N pages, each carrying its own PageLine — e.g. 10k one-cell rows go from ~230 pages to ~115k pages purely from the attribute. The new normalizer removes the non-terminating/1e9 cases but not the amplification, and no aggregate guard (max total table height or max page count) exists in the paginator. Grading by impact (reader-side hang/OOM); confidence low because the payload cost of the rows themselves limits the blow-up.

verdict.reason: The absence itself is factually accurate — I confirmed there is no aggregate page-count/total-height cap anywhere: the clamp is strictly per-entry (row-height.ts:35-46) applied per row (table-layout.ts:251-258), and paginateLayout's split loop (pagination.ts:94-147) plus the final page push (pagination.ts:189-194) impose no ceiling; a repo-wide MAX_* sweep and checks of the CRDT read boundary (yorkie-doc-store.ts:454-470), backend serializer (docs-tree.ts:158-159) and paste path (clipboard.ts:296-298) turned up no such guard. It is nonetheless not a Correctness-lens defect. The paginator's output is arithmetically CORRECT for the input: 10000px is the sanctioned ceiling ("~10 letter pages", row-height.ts:1-8), so a row declared that tall genuinely occupies ~12 pages of an ~864px content box, and N such rows genuinely occupy ~12N pages. There is no wrong condition, off-by-one, inverted logic, missing guard, or non-termination — fragHeight is always >0 (pagination.ts:129-134) so the loop provably terminates, which row-height.test.ts:89-110 pins. That is a different class from the Infinity/1e9 single-row cases the change fixed, which were genuine logic defects. Cost is linear with a fixed ≤12x constant: each ~12-page row needs a real tree row, and findRowSplitHeight is scoped to that row's own cells (table-layout.ts:471-534), so no super-linear blowup. The 115k-page scenario needs an adversarial 10k-row document at the ceiling, not any normal-use path. Asking for a global page/height budget to blunt a hostile collaborator's document is resource-limit hardening against malicious input — the Security lens's lane, explicitly excluded here — and under this rubric's ladder it is neither normal-use-reachable wrong behavior nor an input outside the feature's stated range.
